VIDEO.title: The Most Overlooked Line in the Great Commission
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Matthew 28 · Episode 55 (#58 of 58 in the playlist)
SUMMARY: The teacher reads all of Matthew 28. After the Sabbath, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary come to the grave. An earthquake, an angel like lightning, the stone rolled away, the guards like dead men. 'He is not here, for He has risen, just as He said.' Jesus meets the women, and they take hold of His feet and worship Him. The chief priests and elders pay the soldiers to say the disciples stole the body. In Galilee, on the mountain Jesus designated, the eleven worship, though some doubt, and Jesus gives the Great Commission.

The other accounts are Mark 16, Luke 24 and John 20 (the earliest manuscripts of Mark lack 16:9-20). No Gospel describes the resurrection itself; it is told through witnesses: an angel, the soldiers, the women and the disciples. The leaders hear the testimony and refuse to believe, though at the cross they had said, 'we will believe in Him' (27:42).

The women are the first to see Him. Because a woman's testimony was not usually accepted in court then, a made-up story would not have put them first, which points to the account's truthfulness. Which mountain is unknown (Tabor? Hermon?). 'Doubted' means wavered or hesitated. The Commission has one command, 'make disciples'; everything else serves it.

Connections: the Sabbath rest (Exodus 16:29; Isaiah 58:13); the angel like Daniel's (Daniel 10:5-6, 12; 7:9) and Ezekiel's living creatures (Ezekiel 1:14); the third day (Hosea 6:2) and Psalm 16:10 as Peter and Paul read it (Acts 2; 13:36-37); 'all authority' and Daniel 7:13-14; the name of God as presence (Numbers 6:27; Exodus 23:21), authority (Deuteronomy 18:19) and power (Psalm 20:1, 5, 7).
The lesson: in Jesus, the disciples possess the power, the authority and the presence of God; therefore they must go and immerse others into this same power, authority and presence.
QUOTES: In Jesus, the disciples possess the power, the authority, and the presence of God. Therefore, they must go and immerse others into this same power, authority, and presence.
Even in post-resurrection, Jesus is still the rabbi, right?
The Great Commission is not something to tread over too quickly. It's something upon which to meditate again and again and again and again.
This is about spending a duration of time with people so they can be baptized into so much more than that.

method.p: In a long command, find the one main verb and ask how every other phrase serves it. In 28:19-20 it is 'make disciples.'

LSB_QUOTES.text: He is not here, for He has risen, just as He said. Come, see the place where He was lying.
Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,
and behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.

left.text: And behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and came and rolled away the stone and sat upon it. And his appearance was like lightning, and his clothing as white as snow.

right.text: His body also was like beryl, his face had the appearance of lightning, his eyes were like flaming torches, his arms and feet like the gleam of burnished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.

lines.text: Daniel's angel also says, 'Do not be afraid' (Daniel 10:12). Ezekiel's living creatures move 'with the appearance of lightning' (Ezekiel 1:14), and the Ancient of Days wears clothing 'like white snow' (Daniel 7:9): perhaps a sign of the closeness angels enjoy with God.
The women waited until after the Sabbath (Exodus 16:29; Isaiah 58:13): grief and reverence at once.

TOMB.title: He has risen, just as He said

src.text: And behold, Jesus met them and said, “Greetings!” And they came up and took hold of His feet and worshiped Him. Then Jesus *said to them, “Do not be afraid; go and report to My brothers to leave for Galilee, and there they will see Me.”

lines.text: No one describes the resurrection itself. The soldiers are the first potential witnesses, but they never see Him. The first to see Jesus alive are the women, then the disciples.
A woman's testimony was not usually accepted in court in the first century. Had the disciples invented the story, they would not have made women the first witnesses.
The video suggests Matthew tells verses 2-4 before verse 1 in time, comparing Mark 16:1, where the women come with spices to anoint Him.

left.text: And when they had assembled with the elders and took counsel together, they gave a large sum of money to the soldiers, and said, “You are to say, ‘His disciples came by night and stole Him away while we were asleep.’

right.text: “He saved others; He cannot save Himself. He is the King of Israel; let Him now come down from the cross, and we will believe in Him.

lines.text: The leaders are witnesses too: they hear the guards' report and still refuse to believe. Matthew shows they never meant to believe.

src.text: But the eleven disciples proceeded to Galilee, to the mountain which Jesus had designated. And when they saw Him, they worshiped Him; but some doubted.

lines.text: Which mountain? Tabor, another hill in Galilee, or Hermon just to the north? We are not told. A teacher the video cites notes that the trip back would retrace places of earlier lessons: even after the resurrection, Jesus is still the rabbi.
'Doubted' means to waver or hesitate: perhaps they did not yet know how to react to seeing Him alive.

left.text: For You will not forsake my soul to Sheol; / You will not give Your Holy One over to see corruption.

right.text: For David, after he had served the purpose of God in his own generation, fell asleep and was laid among his fathers and saw corruption; but He whom God raised did not see corruption.

lines.text: The resurrection of the Messiah had precedent: 'He will raise us up on the third day' (Hosea 6:2). Peter (Acts 2) and Paul (Acts 13) read Psalm 16:10 as fulfilled in Jesus, since David's body did see corruption.

left.text: And Jesus came up and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,

right.text: And to Him was given dominion, / Glory, and a kingdom, / That all the peoples, nations, and men of every tongue / Might serve Him.

lines.text: All authority, all the nations, all that I commanded. In the Greek the one command is 'make disciples'; going, baptizing and teaching serve it. That is a slow, intentional process, like Jesus' own with His disciples.
'Therefore' ties verse 19 to verse 18: the mission rests on Jesus' authority. 'I am with you always' is fulfilled through the Spirit (John 14-17; Acts 2) until He returns.

src.text: Yahweh bless you, and keep you; / Yahweh make His face shine on you, / And be gracious to you; / Yahweh lift up His face on you, / And give you peace.’ So they shall invoke My name on the sons of Israel, and I then will bless them.”

lines.text: The name of God is not a phrase to close a prayer but His power, authority and presence. In the priestly blessing, God's name on Israel is His face shining on them: His presence.
Of the angel sent before Israel, God says, 'My name is in him' (Exodus 23:21). See also Exodus 33:18-19, 1 Kings 8:27-29 and Joel 2:32.

NAME.title: Authority and power
NAME.stamp: In the name of our God

left.text: And it will be that whoever will not listen to My words which he shall speak in My name, I Myself will require it of him.

right.text: Some boast in chariots and some in horses, / But we will boast in the name of Yahweh, our God.

lines.text: The prophet like Moses speaks 'in My name': with God's authority. David speaks of God's saving power as His name: 'May the name of the God of Jacob set you securely on high!' (Psalm 20:1).
So to baptize 'in the name' is to immerse people into the power, authority and presence of God, a whole way of living, not a magic phrase.

TERMS.def: Jesus' charge in 28:18-20 to make disciples of all the nations.
In Scripture, God's power, authority and presence, not only a word spoken.
The short distance one might walk on the Sabbath (Acts 1:12).
The close of this age at Jesus' return.

WORDS.gloss: To raise, wake; passive, to rise.
To make disciples; the main command of 28:19. Look up: BDAG, μαθητεύω.

BACKGROUND.p: Some wealthy tombs near Jerusalem were closed with a large disc-shaped stone set in a groove; most used a block stone. Either way, moving it took several people.
Josephus records that the law of his day did not accept women's testimony (Antiquities 4.219), which makes the Gospels' choice of women as first witnesses striking.
By the first century the Sabbath limit was fixed at a short walk, 'a Sabbath day's journey' (Acts 1:12), later set at 2,000 cubits in rabbinic law.

DEBATES.p: Grammatically 'make disciples' is the only imperative; 'go' is a participle. Many still read 'go' as carrying the force of a command alongside it.
Some suggest Tabor, some Hermon, others the hills near the Sea of Galilee. Matthew does not say.
The video reads 'the age' as the messianic age that lasts until Jesus returns; others speak of 'this age' giving way to 'the age to come.' Both point to His return.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: Mark 16:1 names three women: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome (the captions garble this).
Exodus 16:29 and Isaiah 58:13 are about Sabbath rest generally; the fixed walking limit (Acts 1:12) comes from later tradition.
That Matthew tells verses 2-4 before verse 1 in time is the video's inference from comparing the Gospels.
The longer ending of Mark (16:9-20) is missing from the earliest manuscripts, so the video's Mark 16:12-20 reference rests on it.

QUESTIONS: Why do you think no Gospel describes the moment of the resurrection itself?
What does it tell you that women were the first witnesses?
Why might some of the eleven still have doubted on the mountain?
If 'make disciples' is the one command, how should going, baptizing and teaching serve it?
What does the name of God mean in Numbers 6, Deuteronomy 18 and Psalm 20?
When you feel far from God, how could Romans 6:11 reorient your perspective?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The lesson: in Jesus, the disciples possess the power, the authority and the presence of God, and they must go and immerse others into the same. When we feel far from God, our position has not changed; our perspective needs reminding. Paul's answer is to consider ourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus (Romans 6:2-4, 11), a daily practice. Jesus has all authority today, and His power and presence are ours, whatever we feel. Making disciples is more than a few sentences about the gospel: it means spending time with people so they are baptized into so much more. This closes the Matthew study.

Which mountain is unknown (Tabor? Hermon?). 'Doubted' means wavered or hesitated. The Commission has one command, 'make disciples'; everything else serves it.

In a long command, find the one main verb and ask how every other phrase serves it. In 28:19-20 it is 'make disciples.'

   (video) Daniel's angel also says, 'Do not be afraid' (Daniel 10:12). Ezekiel's living creatures move 'with the appearance of lightning' (Ezekiel 1:14), and the Ancient of Days wears clothing 'like white snow' (Daniel 7:9): perhaps a sign of the closeness angels enjoy with God. (Daniel 10:12; Ezekiel 1:14; Daniel 7:9)

   First witnesses Matthew 28:9-10: "And behold, Jesus met them and said, “Greetings!” And they came up and took hold of His feet and worshiped Him. Then Jesus *said to them, “Do not be afraid; go and report to My brothers to leave for Galilee, and there they will see Me.”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+28:9-10

   (video) A woman's testimony was not usually accepted in court in the first century. Had the disciples invented the story, they would not have made women the first witnesses.

## Key people
- Mary Magdalene and the other Mary: Wait out the Sabbath, find the empty tomb, and are the first to see Jesus. [Background] Mark adds Salome and names the other Mary as the mother of James (Mark 16:1).
- The angel of the Lord: Rolls away the stone and tells the women not to be afraid. [Background] Like the figures in Daniel's visions (Daniel 10:6).
- The guards: First potential witnesses, who never see Him; then paid to lie. [Background] They answered to the chief priests and to Pilate (27:65-66).
- The eleven: Worship on the mountain, though some doubt, and receive the Commission. [Background] Judas is gone (27:5).

## Places [Background]
- Jerusalem (named in the video): The empty tomb, and the guards' report to the chief priests (28:11).
- Mount Tabor (named in the video): One suggestion for 'the mountain which Jesus had designated' (28:16).
- Mount Hermon (named in the video): Another suggestion, just north of Galilee; we are not told.
- Capernaum: Jesus' Galilean base, where many earlier lessons were given (4:13).

## Key terms
- Great Commission: Jesus' charge in 28:18-20 to make disciples of all the nations.
- The name of God: In Scripture, God's power, authority and presence, not only a word spoken.
- Sabbath day's journey: The short distance one might walk on the Sabbath (Acts 1:12). [Background]
- The end of the age: The close of this age at Jesus' return.

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Rolling-stone tombs: Some wealthy tombs near Jerusalem were closed with a large disc-shaped stone set in a groove; most used a block stone. Either way, moving it took several people.
- Women as witnesses: Josephus records that the law of his day did not accept women's testimony (Antiquities 4.219), which makes the Gospels' choice of women as first witnesses striking.
- Sabbath travel: By the first century the Sabbath limit was fixed at a short walk, 'a Sabbath day's journey' (Acts 1:12), later set at 2,000 cubits in rabbinic law.

## Early witnesses [Background: sourced]
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "And indeed when should they have stolen Him? On the Sabbath? And how? For it was not lawful so much as to go out." Homilies on Matthew 89, on 28:13. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "And if some doubted, herein again admire their truthfulness, how they conceal not even their shortcomings up to the last day." Homilies on Matthew 90, on 28:17. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "For tell me not, says He, of the difficulty of the things: for I am with you, who make all things easy." Homilies on Matthew 90, on 28:20. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- How many commands? Grammatically 'make disciples' is the only imperative; 'go' is a participle. Many still read 'go' as carrying the force of a command alongside it.
- Which mountain? Some suggest Tabor, some Hermon, others the hills near the Sea of Galilee. Matthew does not say.
- The end of the age The video reads 'the age' as the messianic age that lasts until Jesus returns; others speak of 'this age' giving way to 'the age to come.' Both point to His return.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- Mark 16:1 names three women: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome (the captions garble this).
- Exodus 16:29 and Isaiah 58:13 are about Sabbath rest generally; the fixed walking limit (Acts 1:12) comes from later tradition.
- That Matthew tells verses 2-4 before verse 1 in time is the video's inference from comparing the Gospels.
- The longer ending of Mark (16:9-20) is missing from the earliest manuscripts, so the video's Mark 16:12-20 reference rests on it.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. Why do you think no Gospel describes the moment of the resurrection itself?
2. What does it tell you that women were the first witnesses?
3. Why might some of the eleven still have doubted on the mountain?
4. If 'make disciples' is the one command, how should going, baptizing and teaching serve it?
5. What does the name of God mean in Numbers 6, Deuteronomy 18 and Psalm 20?
6. When you feel far from God, how could Romans 6:11 reorient your perspective?

## Application
- (video) The lesson: in Jesus, the disciples possess the power, the authority and the presence of God, and they must go and immerse others into the same. When we feel far from God, our position has not changed; our perspective needs reminding. Paul's answer is to consider ourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus (Romans 6:2-4, 11), a daily practice. Jesus has all authority today, and His power and presence are ours, whatever we feel. Making disciples is more than a few sentences about the gospel: it means spending time with people so they are baptized into so much more. This closes the Matthew study.
- Study note (added): name one person you could walk with this year, meeting regularly to read Scripture and pray together.
